Action Plan:
1. Encourage liberal oral fluid intake; purchase and use an oral re-hydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as directed to replace electrolytes lost through diarrhea.
2. Take Paracetamol as needed for fever or generalized weakness (dose/route/frequency not documented).
3. Remain off work and other public activities until ≥24–48 hr diarrhea-free; reassess ability to resume normal duties after that period.
4. Safety-net: if diarrhea persists beyond 5–7 days, worsens, or if new red-flag symptoms (e.g., blood in stool, severe abdominal pain, high fever, inability to keep fluids down) develop, patient to re-contact clinic for review.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Watery diarrhea for 3 days, frequency ~5–6 times/day; began with two episodes of vomiting (now resolved).  
• Associated symptoms: Subjective dehydration, weakness, reduced appetite; no abdominal pain, no visible blood in stool, no current fever, no headache or myalgias.  
• Onset/context: Symptoms started at home while working; no recalled high-risk food intake or unwell contacts.  
• Past medical history: Asthma.  
• Medications: Blue inhaler (salbutamol) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Father – hypertension, deceased from bowel cancer; Mother – type 2 diabetes.  
• Social history: Lives alone; software engineer; non-smoker; infrequent social alcohol use.

Objective:
• Telehealth consultation – no in-person examination; vitals not recorded.  
• No laboratory or imaging investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute watery diarrhea
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Viral gastroenteritis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Bacterial food-borne infection, medication-related diarrhea, irritable bowel syndrome flare.
   - Investigations planned: None at present; consider stool culture and blood work if no improvement within 1 week or if red-flag symptoms appear.
   - Treatment planned: Oral re-hydration solution (Dioralyte); maintain high oral fluid intake; Paracetamol PRN for fever/aches; temporary work exclusion until 24–48 hr symptom-free.
   - Relevant referrals: Not required at this stage; follow-up with primary care if symptoms persist or worsen.

2. Asthma (background)
   - Assessment: Stable, not contributing to current presentation.
   - Investigations planned: None.
   - Treatment planned: Continue blue inhaler PRN.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs (BP, HR, temperature), abdominal examination findings, full medication reconciliation (names/doses), confirmation of stool color/odor, vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor filler words but overall comprehensible.
